findings.title: Invalid Ruby syntax prevents rendering existing discussions
findings.body: The template closes its conditional with `end if`, leaving a trailing `if` without a condition. This is invalid Ruby syntax in the ERB-generated code, so requests that find an existing embedded topic fail with a template compilation error instead of displaying the discussion. Close the conditional with just `end` and exercise this path with view rendering enabled.

findings.title: Imported feed HTML is persisted without sanitization
findings.body: Feed contents pass through Nokogiri URL rewriting, which does not sanitize HTML, and are saved with the raw_html cook method. Post#cook then returns this HTML unchanged, and the embed template renders post.cooked with `raw`. A feed entry containing a script or an event handler therefore becomes stored XSS on the forum origin. The appended source URL is also interpolated directly into HTML. Sanitize the complete imported fragment and escape the source link before persisting it.

findings.title: RSS entries without content abort the entire poll
findings.body: The poller unconditionally calls `scrub` on `i.content`. Ordinary RSS feeds can provide article text only in `description`, with no content element, so this value can be nil. Such an entry raises an exception and stops importing all subsequent entries; retries are disabled for this job. Support description-only entries and handle entries without either field explicitly.

findings.title: Relative URL conversion corrupts protocol-relative links
findings.body: Every href starting with `/` is rewritten onto the article host, including protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/file`. This produces `http://article-host/cdn.example.com/file` rather than preserving the CDN host. The image branch has the same problem, while path-relative references such as `images/photo.jpg` are not resolved at all and consequently load from the forum origin. Resolve references against the full source URL using URI joining instead of stripping leading slashes.

findings.title: Redirects bypass the retrieval host restriction
findings.body: TopicRetriever checks only the host of the initial embed URL, but `open(url)` follows HTTP redirects without checking their destinations. An allowed-host URL that redirects to another host, including an internal HTTP service, causes the background worker to fetch that service and potentially publish its response as a topic. Validate each redirect destination and enforce restrictions on resolved addresses before connecting, rather than relying on the initial hostname check.
